analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Birla Fashion has been persistently loss-making for five of the last six years, burning through capital with negative ROE of -10.9% and rising finance costs of INR 608 Cr in FY25, while operating in a fashion retail segment under direct e-commerce disruption. This is the opposite of what I look for — a leveraged, loss-making business in a structurally challenged sector.
key_strengths: Operating cash flow positive all 5 years (INR 644–1,644 Cr range) — suggests the core store operations generate cash before lease and finance costs
Strong brand portfolio (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England) with meaningful pricing power in premium menswear
Forward P/E of 10.34x could look attractive IF the company ever turns profitable — but that is a very large if
key_risks: Persistently loss-making: net profit was negative in FY20, FY21, FY22, FY23, FY24, FY25 — INR 456 Cr loss in FY25 alone
Finance costs at INR 608 Cr in FY25 and rising at 18% CAGR — debt-funded expansion in a business that cannot earn its cost of capital
E-commerce disruption is real and accelerating in fashion — fast fashion platforms (Myntra, Meesho, Zudio) are eating the middle market where ABFRL competes
red_flags: ROE of -10.9% and ROCE of -2.87% — the business is actively destroying shareholder value; I avoid any business with negative ROE
Revenue dropped from INR 12,418 Cr (FY23) to INR 6,441 Cr (FY24) — likely due to demerger of ethnic brands, but creates enormous uncertainty about the base business
Promoter holding at 46.61% — below 50%, below my 55% floor; the Aditya Birla Group has multiple capital allocation priorities and ABFRL may not be the focus
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have a simple rule: I do not own loss-making businesses. ABFRL has lost money in five of the last six years, and the losses are substantial — INR 736 Cr in FY24, INR 456 Cr in FY25. Finance costs have exploded from INR 225 Cr to INR 608 Cr as the company borrowed to fund expansion, demergers, and acquisitions of luxury ethnic brands (Sabyasachi, Tarun Tahiliani). The EV/EBITDA of 197x reflects that reported EBITDA is an illusion — Ind AS 116 lease accounting inflates EBITDA while true profitability after rent and finance costs is deeply negative.

Fashion retail is one of the businesses I would most want to avoid — high working capital, fast inventory cycles, trend sensitivity, and now structural disruption from e-commerce and value fashion (Zudio, etc.). The brands are good, but good brands in a bad business still make a bad investment. At P/B of 1.24x the stock looks cheap on paper, but book value is being eroded every year by ongoing losses. I see no floor on the downside here without a clear path to profitability.
